standard.title: Variables and Formulas
standard.description: recognise and use variables to represent everyday formulas algebraically and substitute values into formulas to determine an unknown
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can find unknown values in equations involving brackets and combinations of operations, and recognise rules in growing patterns (from AC9M6A01, AC9M6A02). Students understand that a letter can represent an unknown.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise variables as quantities that can change, represent everyday formulas algebraically, and substitute values to determine unknowns.

nodes.label: Variables as generalised quantities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise that variables represent quantities that can change, and distinguish a variable from an unknown constant.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the variables in a given formula and describe what each represents in context.
nodes.typical_width: Link variables to the attributes they model; explain the difference between a variable (can take many values) and a specific unknown (one value to find).
wider: Investigate how the same letter variable is used differently in different formulas (e.g. A for area in one, for amplitude in another) — variables are context-specific labels.
Explore formulas from other subjects: distance = speed × time; explore what each variable represents.

response_modes.reason: Students entering Y7 typically treat all letters as 'the unknown x to solve for'. The variable-as-generalised-quantity concept requires multiple formula contexts to become stable.

success_criteria: Correctly identifies what each variable represents in a given formula.
Explains the difference between a variable that can take many values and a specific unknown.
Does not treat all variables as things to 'solve for'.

nodes.label: Substituting values into formulas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students substitute given numerical values into a formula and calculate the result.
nodes.minimum_width: Given a formula and values for all but one variable, substitute and evaluate.
nodes.typical_width: Substitute values into formulas from practical contexts (area, perimeter, wage, density); evaluate correctly including with fractions and decimals.
wider: Substitute values into formulas from science and everyday life (e.g. heart rate formula, body mass index) and interpret the result in context.
Investigate Country/Place formulas: investigate formulas used in Indigenous land management or navigation contexts.

response_modes.reason: Substitution is a mechanical skill that requires fluency before finding unknowns. Errors here are typically arithmetic (not algebraic) but propagate into node 3.

nodes.hinge_reason: Arithmetic errors during substitution propagate directly into Node 3 — students who cannot substitute correctly cannot find unknowns, since the finding-unknown step builds on a correctly evaluated substitution.
success_criteria: Correctly substitutes values into a formula and evaluates.
Applies correct order of operations during substitution.
Does not multiply the coefficient by the variable label (e.g. does not treat 3A as 3×'the letter A' rather than 3 times the value of A).

nodes.label: Finding an unknown by substitution and backtracking
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students determine the value of an unknown variable in a formula by substituting known values and solving.
nodes.minimum_width: Given a formula with one unknown and all other values provided, find the unknown by substituting and solving.
nodes.typical_width: Find unknowns in formulas in practical contexts (e.g. find the base wage given total wage and overtime details); verify by substituting back.
wider: Compare finding unknowns using substitution + backtracking vs formal algebraic rearrangement — note both methods are valid.
Apply to a range of real formulas: perimeter to find a missing side, density formula to find mass or volume.

response_modes.reason: Finding an unknown brings together variable understanding, substitution, and arithmetic operations simultaneously. The coordinated application is the learning.

success_criteria: Correctly finds an unknown in a formula given all other values.
Verifies the solution by substituting back into the formula.
Interprets the result in context (with units and meaning).
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Advancing students can explore both substitution/backtracking and formal rearrangement as equivalent methods, and apply to a range of real formulas — connecting algebra to science and everyday contexts.
